facts.content: Patient experiences burning and stinging with urination for a few days.
facts.source_text: CC: Burning/stinging w/ urination x few days

facts.content: Patient has lower abdominal crampy pain with voiding.
facts.source_text: Lower abd crampy pain w/ voiding

facts.content: Patient had a small episode of hematuria today.
Patient has a history of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
Patient tried over-the-counter bicarbonate without relief.
Patient is allergic to Clindamycin, causing swelling.
Patient denies family history of renal, urinary, or gastrointestinal diseases.
Patient is a college student in biology and lives with friends.
Patient consumes alcohol socially on weekends.
Assessment indicates acute uncomplicated cystitis with dysuria for a few days, lower abdominal cramps, and malodorous urine.
facts.source_text: Acute uncomplicated cystitis — dysuria x few days, lower abd cramps, malodorous urine

facts.content: Prescribe Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.
facts.source_text: Nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim: 1 tab BID x 3 days

facts.content: Increase hydration and consider optional cranberry juice.
Patient should avoid intercourse until symptoms resolve and continue using condoms.
facts.source_text: Avoid intercourse until sx resolve; continue condoms

facts.content: Patient should call or return to clinic if not improved by the end of the week, or if fever, back pain, or systemic illness develop.
facts.source_text: if not improved by end of week → call/RTC; sooner if fever, back pain, or systemically unwell
